narrative:
Method.

- **Images.** The base commit was exported with `git archive`. Both trees
  were configured with the shared configuration script and built with `-j 6`
  under `~/.cache/sunstoneos/build/gpu-recognition/`. Four default OS
  variants were built at each commit: supervised, resident, resident with the
  I2S microphone and resident with the Bluetooth headset. `llvm-objcopy-21 -O
  binary` gave the loadable bytes and `llvm-size-21 -A` the section sizes. The
  GPU linear image was built at the change only, resident, with the pinned
  GPU firmware and the bench models (`~/.cache/sunstoneos/inputs/mimus-bench`),
  for the A76 pair, twice: with the pinned engine, which has no hook
  header, and with the engine of mimus commit `9c57286b7`, which declares
  and implements the hook. "With the engine's hook" below gives the later
  measurements with that engine.
- **Session in QEMU.** `checks/pvr-mimus-service.py` built a two-core
  FreeRTOS image for QEMU's `virt` machine. It constructs the session with
  the image's `a733_gpu_reserved_prepare` and `a733_gpu_mimus_prepare` over
  the production pools, runs the kernel ring through
  `platform/a733/gpu_memory.c` and delivers completions on SPI 95 of QEMU's
  GIC through `gicv3_spi.c`. A software firmware model, reused from
  `checks/pvr-gpu-service.c`, checks each kick's 96-byte compute command and
  timeline UPDATE; a model task on the second core writes exact sums and tags
  after the duration `placement.py` models for each job on the A76 table.
  An EL0 client task runs OPEN and the bench recording's 204 jobs. Weights
  are synthetic bytes at the real tensor offsets, the output region stays
  writable at EL1 so the model can store into it, and GPU registers are model
  callbacks, whose accesses were counted and costed at two `DSB SY` each, as
  `gpu_backend.c` issues them. Counts come from traced runs with one
  instruction per translation block (`-d exec,nochain -dfilter` over all 154
  `dsb sy` sites and the counted function entries, `-icount shift=0`), split
  into per-job windows at a marker function, and from `--wrap` counters.
  The traced bench runs divide by the 204 jobs; their worker wake-ups use the
  instruction counter as the guest clock, and a run at real time is given
  beside them.
- **Engine contract.** `checks/gpu-recognition-engine.py` built the hook, the
  dispatcher and a model of the mimus engine for the host with
  AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, without the hook header
  and with it.
- **Dispatcher, mapping checks, pools and gate.** `checks/os-image-dispatch.py
  --configure-from` the resident build ran the placement tables, the C
  dispatcher model over the bench call list with exact sums and over the
  longest accepted input, the mapping-check, stop-detail and pool-replay
  cases, the recognizer patch chains and the CMake gate cases.
- **Time model.** `apps/os/placement.py --summary`, issue-bound and with
  `--load-cycles 200` and `400`.
- **Other GPU images.** The existing `pvr-gpu-service.py` (cases 1 to 6 on
  the service, native-memory and asynchronous-power models),
  `pvr-gpu-irq.py`, `pvr-gpu-freelist-service.py` and
  `pvr-compute-service.py` checks, and the GPU render image's link, at the
  change. `checks/device-memory-capacity.py` ran its QEMU golden comparison,
  including the read-only output view, and scanned the GPU linear build's
  images.

The base commit has no GPU path in the OS image, so its rows below are the
CPU-only image or the design's stated baseline.

Baseline commit for the comparison: 959bccd (bringup merged into the design commit).

narrative:
With the engine's hook.

These runs use mimus commit `9c57286b7` (the hook engine) and, for
comparison, the pinned mimus commit `3e05158e3`, at the change and at its
base, commit `9e631433`. QEMU runs use the two-core `virt` image of
[mimus-smp.md](../mimus-smp.md) with the bench recording. Under
`-icount shift=0` the guest clock advances one nanosecond per instruction, so
each "us" figure that the image prints counts thousands of instructions
retired on both cores, including the FreeRTOS idle loop of a core with no
work; the figures are not elapsed time.

The pinned engine ran the packed GEMM's read-out on the other worker by
default, and the hook engine does not. The single-A55 board baseline had no
other worker, so that offload never ran there, and the design's modeled
recognition rows stay derived from that baseline.

image: GPU linear OS image, host check
hypothesis: Transport and maintenance barriers per GPU job match the counts read from the code.
prediction:
Barriers per job, read from the code at baseline commit 0fd1b51 with an empty firmware queue on each check. Each gpu_memory.c write and each GPU register access issues two DSB SY, and each gpu_memory.c read one. burst() would run further steps after the kick and after the post, so the service ends a burst once a ready session has nothing to submit and the interrupt is re-enabled; a job takes two worker steps.

| Step | Source | `DSB SY` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Slot to kick | Interrupt mask at step start (`gicv3_spi_mask`) | 1 |
| | Firmware-queue check: two interrupt-status reads (4), empty receive (5), kernel-ring return poll (6) | 15 |
| | Client-ring space check: acquire, two control reads | 3 |
| | Client-ring command writes | 0 |
| | Client-ring publish | 1 |
| | `pvr_ccb_submit`: control check (5), command and return writes (4), two releases, write offset (2), kick (2), completion barrier | 16 |
| | Total to the kick; then re-enable (`gicv3_spi_rearm`, 2) | 36 + 2 |
| Interrupt to post | Handler mask | 1 |
| | Firmware-queue check with the interrupt pending: as above, plus the interrupt clear (2) and the job's kernel-ring return (1) | 18 |
| | Total to the post; then re-enable | 19 + 2 |
| Per firmware event in a batch | `pvr_ccb_receive` | 11 |
| Per timed wake while the job runs | Mask, firmware-queue check, re-enable | 19 |

A job therefore costs 59 transport and 6 maintenance barriers, plus 19 per
timed wake and 11 per firmware event. The GPU runtime design
([gpu-runtime.md](gpu-runtime.md)) owns the reduction to lighter barriers in
`gpu_memory.c` and `gicv3_spi.c`, which needs the board qualification of
[shared-helpers.md](../shared-helpers.md); "Left out" gives its cost here.
conclusion: The QEMU host check counts 57 transport barriers per job (gpu_memory.c 37, mask and re-enable 6, client ring 4, GPU register accesses 10; 58.9 with modeled durations), 18 per timed wake and 11 per firmware event; the code reading gave 59, 19 and 11. The kick step costs 32 DSB SY plus 4 for register accesses and the step that posts the record 14 plus 6. Lighter transport barriers are left out (see the design).

hypothesis: Some placement or lever meets the recognition goal of 0.05 times the audio duration (0.4435 s for the bench recording).
prediction:
The goal allows 0.4435 s from PCM to text for the bench recording. Attention and the remaining stages took 4.582 s on one A55 at 494 MHz (mimus.md). Two A76 cores at 2,002 MHz, each doing twice an A55's work per clock and scaling perfectly, would take 0.283 s for them; the A55 pair 2.291 s.

The goal allows 0.4435 s from PCM to text for the bench recording. With the
other stages at 0.283 s on the A76 pair, the linear stage may take at most
0.161 s; the best split takes 0.535 s, and recognition at 0.818 s is 1.84
times the goal (0.092 against 0.05 times the audio duration). The A55 pair
cannot meet the goal at all, because its other stages alone take 2.291 s, so
admission of the A76 cores is the first requirement. The same model on the
A76 pair gives:

| Lever (owner) | Linear stage | Recognition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CPU only, no GPU (the CPU baseline of the model) | 0.920 s | 1.203 s, 0.136× |
| None | 0.535 s | 0.818 s, 0.092× |
| GPU at 800 MHz (GPU power and thermal owner) | 0.385 s | 0.668 s |
| 1.75 GPU instructions per MAC (kernel design) | 0.394 s | 0.677 s |
| NEON int32-lane accumulation at 4× the CPU rate (mimus engine) | 0.220 s | 0.503 s |
| 800 MHz and 4× | 0.187 s | 0.470 s, 0.053× |
| 800 MHz, 1.75 instructions per MAC and 4× | 0.157 s | 0.440 s, 0.0496× |

Only all three levers together reach the goal, and only if the other stages
scale perfectly. No GPU operating point above 400 MHz is recorded, the
gpu-mimus measurements record no program below 3.39 instructions per MAC, and
the CPU factor is unmeasured.

The GPU rows exclude the hook's validation of every GPU sum (`SumsEqual` in
`apps/os/gpu_hook.cc`), a scalar loop on the recognizer core alone that
costs about 1.9 s per recording on the A76 pair. While it stays, the GPU
linear stage takes about 2.4 s, slower than the 0.920 s of CPU only;
splitting it across both workers or vectorizing it would shorten that until
the board items let it go. The read-out's memory traffic, about 13 GB/s from
just-invalidated lines on the A76 pair, is unmeasured until the board run.

hypothesis: The hook's scalar comparison of every GPU sum with an int64 CPU sum costs more than the GPU saves until the board items let it go.
prediction:
Until the board items on GPU cache invalidation at job start, cross-core code
writes, GPU read-only enforcement and fault-slot retention across a WDT0
reset pass, the hook compares every GPU sum with an int64 sum that a scalar
CPU loop computes from the same codes and weights, before it returns the job
to the engine; the comparison is unconditional and has no build switch. A
mismatch is handled as a missing tag. At two cycles per MAC the check costs about 60 ms
for the largest job (62,447,616 MACs) at 2,002 MHz, about 1.9 s per bench
recording on the A76 pair (1.89 G GPU MACs) and about 15 s on the A55 pair at
494 MHz (3.76 G GPU MACs).

The GPU rows exclude the hook's validation of every GPU sum (`SumsEqual` in
`apps/os/gpu_hook.cc`), a scalar loop on the recognizer core alone that
costs about 1.9 s per recording on the A76 pair. While it stays, the GPU
linear stage takes about 2.4 s, slower than the 0.920 s of CPU only;
